title: Cohomology and flat base change
statement:
Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X' & \xrightarrow{g'} & X\\[-2pt]
\downarrow{\scriptstyle f'} & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle f}\\[-2pt]
S' & \xrightarrow{g} & S
\end{array}
$$

be a cartesian diagram of schemes, let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module with $\mathcal{F}'=(g')^*\mathcal{F}$, and assume $g$ is flat and $f$
is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then the base change map

$$
g^*R^if_*\mathcal{F}\;\longrightarrow\;R^if'_*\mathcal{F}'
$$

is an isomorphism for all $i\ge0$; if $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, $S'=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$,
then

$$
H^i(X,\mathcal{F})\otimes_AB\;\cong\;H^i(X',\mathcal{F}')\qquad\text{for all }i .
$$

proof.text: Assume $S=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, $S'=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ and $X$ separated. Choose a finite affine cover $\mathcal U$ of $X$. Every finite intersection is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection], and its pullback is affine. By [lem-pc-cech-computes], the two alternating Cech complexes compute $H^i(X,\mathcal F)$ and $H^i(X',\mathcal F')$. On every intersection the affine pullback-section formula [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] gives $\Gamma(U_J,\mathcal F)\otimes_A B\cong\Gamma((U_J)_B,\mathcal F')$; [lem-pc-base-change-map-cech] says the maps commute with each restriction and alternating differential and realize the canonical base-change map. The cover is finite, so tensoring commutes with its finite products. Thus its Cech complex after base change is the original complex tensored with $B$, and [lem-pc-flat-tensor-complex-cohom] identifies their cohomology. This proves the canonical map $H^i(X,\mathcal F)\otimes_A B\to H^i(X',\mathcal F')$ is an isomorphism for every $i$.

proof.text: For general quasi-separated $X$, choose a finite affine cover $\mathcal U=(U_1,\ldots,U_t)$. Each finite intersection $U_J$ is a quasi-compact open in the affine $U_{j_0}$: pairwise intersections are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion], and finite intersections of quasi-compact opens in an affine scheme are quasi-compact. Hence $U_J$ is separated, and Step 1 applies to $U_J$ and its restricted quasi-coherent sheaf. Use [lem-sc-cech-spectral] for the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequences of $\mathcal U$ and its pulled-back cover. In a Cech double-complex model, pullback of cochains followed by the map on injective resolutions gives a filtered cochain map from the original total complex tensored with $B$ to the pulled-back total complex; flat pullback is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective], so these totals represent the canonical cohomology pullback. Functoriality of the filtered construction [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] identifies its $E_1^{p,q}$ map with the product over $|J|=p+1$ of the Step 1 maps $H^q(U_J,\mathcal F)\otimes_A B\to H^q((U_J)_B,\mathcal F')$. There are finitely many $J$, so this map is an isomorphism and commutes with the alternating Cech differential by functoriality of restrictions. It is therefore an isomorphism at $E_2$. The filtration has $0\le p<t$ and is finite in each total degree. Apply [lem-pc-flat-filtered-complex-comparison] to conclude that the abutment map $H^i(X,\mathcal F)\otimes_A B\to H^i(X',\mathcal F')$ is an isomorphism for every $i$.

proof.text: For the sheaf assertion, restrict to any affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ in $S$ and affine $V'=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ in $g^{-1}V$; the restricted square has a flat base map and a quasi-compact quasi-separated $f|_{f^{-1}V}$. Both higher direct images are quasi-coherent by [lem-pc-finite-support-hi]. Their higher cohomology over the affine bases vanishes by [lem-pc-affine-vanishing], so the canonical Leray edge isomorphisms of [lem-pc-leray-degenerate-sections] identify their section modules with $H^i(f^{-1}V,\mathcal F)$ and $H^i(f'^{-1}V',\mathcal F')$. Affine pullback of a quasi-coherent module identifies sections of $g^*R^if_*\mathcal F$ over $V'$ with $\Gamma(V,R^if_*\mathcal F)\otimes_A B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections]. The canonical map of Tag 02N7 is the map [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-map-sections]: $g'$ is flat as a base change of $g$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] (applied with the roles of the two factors of $X'=S'\times_SX$ exchanged), and its adjoint sends a cohomology class on $f^{-1}V$ to its pullback on $f'^{-1}V'$. Under the Leray and affine-section identifications this is exactly the map proved invertible in Step 2. The construction of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-map-sections] is a sheaf morphism, so the isomorphisms on affine $V'$ agree on overlaps and prove $g^*R^if_*\mathcal F\to R^if'_*\mathcal F'$ is an isomorphism.
